blocks.heading: Currency conversion
blocks.text: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another. Read its direction before calculating: if one foreign unit equals a stated number of N$, multiply foreign units by that N$ amount to convert into N$, or divide N$ by it to obtain foreign units. Show the units and state any assumption about fees. Do not reverse the rate or use a current market rate when a question supplies a one. A conversion changes the currency expression, not automatically the underlying value of goods.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: At an exchange rate of US$1 = N$20, Tula Goods must pay US$150; ignore fees. N$ required = 150 × 20 = N$3,000. Conversely N$3,000 / 20 gives US$150.
